stem: How many of the maps in the collection use neither the Robinson projection nor the Winkel tripel projection?
stimulus:
A university library holds a collection of 480 world maps. Each map uses exactly one projection. The table shows what percent of the collection uses each projection.

World Maps by Projection
Projection | Percent of collection
Mercator | 22.5%
Robinson | 17.5%
Winkel tripel | 35%
Other | 25%
explanation: "Neither Robinson nor Winkel tripel" means the maps in the other two rows, Mercator and Other. You can add those two percents: $22.5\% + 25\% = 47.5\%$. You can also subtract the two excluded rows from 100%: $100\% - 17.5\% - 35\% = 47.5\%$. Write the percent as a decimal and multiply by the total: $0.475 \times 480 = 228$. Common wrong answers: 252 is the maps that use Robinson or Winkel tripel, which is the opposite of what is asked. 120 and 108 each count only one of the two rows you need. 47.5 is the percent, not the number of maps.

common_errors.why: Added the Robinson and Winkel tripel percents (52.5%) and took 52.5% of 480, so the answer counts maps that use either projection instead of neither.
Took only the Other row: 25% of 480. This leaves out the Mercator maps, which also use neither projection.
Took only the Mercator row: 22.5% of 480. This leaves out the Other maps.
Found the combined percent correctly but entered it as the answer without multiplying by 480.
Took 35% of 480, which is the Winkel tripel maps only.

stem: On how many of the 240 days was precipitation recorded that was not snow?
stimulus: A weather station kept daily records for 240 days. Measurable precipitation was recorded on 35% of those days. On 25% of the days with measurable precipitation, the precipitation was snow. On each of the other precipitation days, the precipitation was something other than snow.
explanation: Work in two steps, and use the right total each time. First find the days with precipitation: $0.35 \times 240 = 84$. The 25% applies to those 84 days, not to all 240. Snow fell on 25% of them, so precipitation that was not snow fell on the other 75%: $0.75 \times 84 = 63$. Common wrong answers: 21 is the snow days, the opposite of what is asked. 84 is all the precipitation days, so you stopped halfway. 180 comes from taking 75% of all 240 days. 156 is the days with no precipitation at all.

common_errors.why: Took 25% of the 84 precipitation days, which counts the snow days instead of the days that were not snow.
Found the precipitation days (35% of 240) and stopped before taking the not-snow part.
Applied the 75% to all 240 days instead of to the 84 precipitation days.
Took 65% of 240, which counts the days with no precipitation.
Took 25% of all 240 days, ignoring that the snow percent applies only to the precipitation days.

stem: How many pages in the archive contain annotations in the composer's own handwriting?
stimulus: A music archive has digitized 2,500 pages of a composer's surviving manuscripts. Researchers found that 0.4% of these pages contain annotations in the composer's own handwriting.
explanation: To change a percent to a decimal, move the decimal point two places left. For 0.4%, that gives 0.004, not 0.4 and not 0.04. Multiply by the total: $0.004 \times 2{,}500 = 10$. As a check, 1% of 2,500 is 25, and 0.4% has to be less than that. Common wrong answers: 1000 comes from treating 0.4% as 0.4, which is 40%. 100 comes from moving the point only one place. 2490 is the pages with no annotations.

common_errors.why: Treated 0.4% as the decimal 0.4 (which is 40%) and computed 0.4 × 2,500.
Moved the decimal point only one place and used 0.04 (which is 4%), so the answer is 4% of 2,500.
Found the 10 annotated pages and subtracted from 2,500, which counts the pages without annotations.
Moved the decimal point three places and used 0.0004.

stem: How many distinct words did the child use at 24 months?
stimulus: A linguist tracked the vocabulary of one child. At 18 months, the child used 84 distinct words. At 24 months, the number of distinct words the child used was 325% of the number used at 18 months.
explanation: Translate the sentence literally. "325% of 84" means $3.25 \times 84$, and that equals 273. Watch the wording. "325% of" a number is different from "increased by 325%." An increase of 325% would mean adding 325% of 84 on top of the original 84. That gives 425% of 84, but this sentence does not say that. Common wrong answers: 357 comes from reading the sentence as an increase of 325%. 189 is how much the vocabulary grew, not the vocabulary at 24 months. 27.3 and 2730 come from moving the decimal point the wrong number of places.

common_errors.why: Read "325% of" as "increased by 325%" and computed 4.25 × 84.
Found the increase in vocabulary (273 − 84, or 225% of 84) instead of the vocabulary at 24 months.
Changed 325% to 0.325 by moving the decimal point three places instead of two.
Changed 325% to 32.5 by moving the decimal point only one place.
